release.title: Labour Force Survey, July 2026
release.highlights: Employment increased by 75,000 (+0.4%) in July 2026 and the employment rate rose 0.1 percentage points to 60.9%. The unemployment rate declined 0.1 percentage points to 6.4%. Employment rose among core-aged people (25 to 54 years old) (+51,000; +0.4%), mostly for women in that age group (+33,000; +0.5%). The unemployment rate for core-aged women fell 0.3 percentage points to 5.2%, while youth unemployment held steady at 12.6%. Employment increased in Ontario (+52,000; +0.6%), British Columbia (+18,000; +0.6%), Manitoba (+5,900; +0.8%), and Nova Scotia (+4,600; +0.9%).

methodology_rules.title: Age-structure confounding in provincial 15+ rate comparisons
methodology_rules.rule: Do not publish raw 15-and-over employment or participation rate gaps across provinces as labour-market differences. Comparing Alberta and Newfoundland and Labrador on the 15+ denominator yields a 13.0 percentage point gap, whereas holding age group to prime working age (25 to 54 years) yields 3.4 points; roughly three-quarters of the 15+ gap is population age structure rather than labour-market conditions.

semantic_rule.explanation: Three-quarters of the raw 15+ provincial employment rate gap reflects population age composition rather than labour-market conditions.

methodology_rules.title: Population denominator precision for gender and age cuts
methodology_rules.rule: When a series is held at Age group = '25 to 54 years' and Gender = 'Women+', prose must name 'core-aged women' rather than 'women' as a whole, and explain that an all-ages comparison would be affected by differing age structures across populations.

methodology_rules.title: Multi-year and long-run endpoint comparisons
methodology_rules.rule: Seasonally adjusted multi-year or long-run comparisons measure cumulative shifts between endpoints, not single-month movements or linear paths. Prose must distinguish share of total employment (which reflects population size plus employment rate) from an employment rate gap.

methodology_rules.title: Coverage subtraction against The Daily mention map
methodology_rules.rule: A candidate bundle that merely restates monthly headline employment or unemployment movements already narrated in The Daily highlights should be skipped with rejection_category='already_in_daily'.

methodology_rules.title: Unverified informal cyclical heuristic
methodology_rules.rule: Draft note (unconfirmed): treat any summer movement in retail trade as structural shift.

candidate_briefs.title: Long-run participation and employment rates among core-aged women (1976 to 2026)
candidate_briefs.summary: Compares July 2026 seasonally adjusted participation and employment rates for core-aged women (25 to 54 years) against the earliest period in Table 14-10-0287-01 (January 1976).

facts.human: as of July 2026, core-aged women's participation rate was 33.8 percentage points higher than in January 1976 (85.6% against 51.8%)
as of July 2026, core-aged women's employment rate was 33.0 percentage points higher than in January 1976 (81.2% against 48.2%)

candidate_briefs.title: Core-aged share of employment and employment-rate gap against young workers (2021 to 2026)
candidate_briefs.summary: Measures the multi-year shift in core-aged workers' share of total employment and the widening employment rate gap between core-aged workers (25 to 54 years) and youth (15 to 24 years) from August 2021 to July 2026.

facts.human: between August 2021 and July 2026, core-aged workers' share of total employment rose from 64.9% to 66.6%
between August 2021 and July 2026, the employment rate gap between core-aged workers and young workers widened by 3.8 percentage points

candidate_briefs.title: Raw 15+ provincial employment-rate gap between Alberta and Newfoundland and Labrador
candidate_briefs.summary: Compares the unadjusted 15-and-over provincial employment rate in Alberta against Newfoundland and Labrador without holding age group to prime working age (25 to 54 years).
candidate_briefs.confound_risk: Raw comparison across Geography on unstandardized aggregate '15 years and over' without age-standardization (violates M1).

facts.human: in July 2026, the 15-and-over employment rate gap between Alberta and Newfoundland and Labrador was 13.0 percentage points (compared with 3.4 points on the prime-age 25 to 54 band)

candidate_briefs.title: Monthly headline employment gain in Ontario and Canada
candidate_briefs.summary: Reports the July 2026 month-over-month employment increase in Ontario (+52,000; +0.6%) and national employment growth (+75,000; +0.4%) that lead The Daily bulletin.

facts.human: in July 2026, employment in Ontario rose by 52,000 (+0.6%) while national employment increased by 75,000 (+0.4%)
